reader.requirement: At --std 85, each LINAGE file gets its own LINAGE-COUNTER holding the body line the device is on; it may be referenced only in Procedure Division statements and never as a receiving operand, must be qualified by file-name when the source program has more than one LINAGE file, is set to 1 by OPEN OUTPUT, and is changed by WRITE only: +1 with no ADVANCING, +n for ADVANCING n / identifier, reset to 1 by ADVANCING PAGE and at every move to a succeeding logical page.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2014 the unqualified-reference count is the source program's OWN LINAGE FDs (a container's GLOBAL LINAGE file is a second candidate only when the program has none); from 2014 the visible set counts

reader.edition-search: grep Edition.(Edition|Year|DialectLevel|Is)|IsActive|CobolVersion in CounterResolver.cs and ReceivingOperandForms.cs (one site, Has(2014)); the runtime counter arms in SequentialConnector.cs (BeginLinagePage, PositionOnLogicalPage, BeginNextLogicalPage) carry no edition test.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only the qualification count in a contained program: at 85 a contained program with its own LINAGE file and a container's GLOBAL LINAGE file may write unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER (it names its own file); at 2023 the same source is refused COBOL5997
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover the receiving-operand refusal, LINAGE-COUNTER as a LINAGE operand and ADVANCING PAGE as overflow; not exercised: counter values after plain / ADVANCING n / identifier / 0 / BEFORE PAGE writes, the OPEN OUTPUT reset, separate counters per file, the qualification requirement and its 85 contained-program arm
